Cheryl Elisabeth Praeger AC FAA is an Australian mathematician. Praeger received BSc (1969) and MSc degrees from the University of Queensland (1974), and a doctorate from the University of Oxford in 1973 under direction of Peter M. Neumann. She has published widely and has advised 27 PhD students (as of March 2018). As of 2026, she is Emeritus Professor of Mathematics at the University of Western Australia. She is best known for her works in group theory, algebraic graph theory and combinatorial designs.
Cheryl Elisabeth Praeger was born in Toowoomba, Queensland.
She completed her high school education at Brisbane Girls Grammar School. After graduating high school, Praeger went to the government vocational guidance section to inquire about how she could further study mathematics.

Terence Chi-Shen Tao AC FAA FRS (Chinese: 陶哲轩; pinyin: Táo Zhéxuān; born 17 July 1975) is an Australian-American mathematician known for his contributions to partial differential equations, combinatorics, harmonic analysis and additive number theory. He was awarded the Fields Medal in 2006 for his contributions to mathematical analysis, discrete mathematics and pure mathematics. He is regarded by many as "the finest mathematician of his generation".
Born to Chinese immigrant parents, Tao was raised in Adelaide, Australia. A child prodigy, he began competing in the International Mathematical Olympiad at age 10 and became the youngest gold medallist in the history of the competition in 1988 at age 13. After earning his doctorate from Princeton University at age 21, he became the youngest full professor in the history of the University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA), where he currently holds the James and Carol Collins Chair in Mathematics.

Tao has made significant contributions to several branches of mathematics, including his collaboration with Ben Green on the Green–Tao theorem, which established that the prime numbers contain arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions, and his work with Emmanuel Candès on the mathematical foundations of compressed sensing. His honours include a MacArthur Fellowship (2007), the Crafoord Prize (2012), the Royal Medal (2014), and the Breakthrough Prize in Mathematics (2015). He was elected a Fellow of the Royal Society in 2007 and appointed a Companion of the Order of Australia in 2026.
